tags.gist: Commends early stakeholder input and supports a risk-proportionate, least-burdensome lifecycle approach where evidence scales with function and consequence, not GenAI's presence.
Supports the two axes and recommends traceability to source material and reversibility of the action as engineerable, verifiable risk modifiers.
Says both escalation errors should be assessed but are incommensurable; manufacturers should prespecify an operating point and report both directions by acuity.
Wants the competency approach to credit architectural controls: hybrid systems with deterministic safety logic can guarantee what generative ones only estimate.
Wants the default comparator to be the median practising clinician or a justified no-device counterfactual, with team performance where humans are in the loop.
Strongly supports trading premarket uncertainty for prespecified monitoring, citing its own production clinician review program.
Says manufacturers can own third-party model changes through containment, pinning with notice, shadow-mode evaluation and regression gates suited to PCCPs.
Supports the framework and wants traceability treated as a formal, verifiable mitigating factor on the consequence axis, since inspectable outputs let errors be caught.
Wants reversibility of the resulting action incorporated, sharpening the line between supervised and autonomous action-taking.
Agrees directiveness depends on substance and context and asks for published worked examples along that continuum covering common function types.
Wants directiveness assessed per characterized output class, such as a bounded disposition set, rather than sentence by sentence.
Says greater directiveness is often safer for emergencies, so assessment should ask whether directiveness fits the situation, not disfavour it.
Urges keeping the paper's balance: presuming categorically that patient-facing functions are riskier would penalize access-expanding tools and embed paternalism.
Would judge patient-facing functions by verifiable safeguards, protocol anchoring, deterministic escalation nets, deferral pathways and comprehension testing, not by audience alone.
Strongly supports bidirectional assessment and wants a prespecified, clinically justified escalation operating point, including deliberate asymmetry for severe cases.
Wants both error directions reported stratified by acuity, since aggregate concordance hides which way errors run.
Wants acceptable escalation error bounds set against documented disagreement among qualified human raters, not an assumed single right answer.
Supports benchmarking then confirmation on the configured device, with evidence scaled by grid position and confirmation not always a prospective study.
Endorses the elements but wants architectural verification plus targeted tests accepted for reproducibility, scope and calibration in hybrid deterministic designs.
Would establish construct validity through clinician-authored protocol-graded cases, correlation with adjudicated real-world performance, and sequestered third-party sets.
Says sponsor benchmarks should not be disfavoured, since a documented one tied to the intended use can beat public assets; address independence by sequestration.
Wants the median practising clinician as default standard, with consensus panels as a ceiling, and interrater variability reported alongside device performance.
Wants justified counterfactual comparators permitted, such as baseline disposition behaviour without the device, with a methodological pathway for identifying them.
Would tie the basis of evaluation to the deployed workflow: team performance where a clinician reviews, device alone when autonomous.
Supports third parties for sequestered datasets and adjudication, wanting multiple accredited bodies per domain with published criteria and capped fees.
Wants sponsors able to self-assess using the same published methods, subject to FDA review, instead of third-party certification.
Wants independence criteria to cover the model developer too, and an LLM adjudicator should share neither developer nor lineage with the component evaluated.
Strongly supports the trade where sponsors precommit to a monitoring plan, triggers, independent adjudication and corrective action, excepting autonomous high-consequence functions.
Confirms the approaches work at production scale, describing weekly clinician review of sampled interactions, regression evaluation and drift monitoring.
Wants review sampling stratified by acuity and interaction pattern, where safety signal concentrates, rather than uniform.
Wants cadence scaled to volume and change frequency, with model, content, context or drift events triggering off-cycle review.
Wants input-population drift monitored as its own signal, since who uses the device can shift performance without any device change.
Supports supervisory agents as a scaling layer flagging cases for review, if evaluated and independent, with clinicians keeping final adjudication.
Wants clarity that institutions monitoring, validating or configuring within the validated envelope are not thereby manufacturers, or they will be deterred.
After losing an upstream vendor, urges architectural containment keeping safety logic outside the third-party model, recognized as a primary mitigation.
Wants version pinning with contractual minimum notice and continued access to prior versions, with FDA articulating these as expected practice.
Wants new model versions run in shadow mode on production traffic and a regression battery, promoted only on prespecified criteria.
Says model version changes passing the regression battery within an envelope are a natural PCCP category needing no new submission.
Supports voluntary master files as structured documentation that would cut duplicative diligence and make review more consistent.
Wants no presumption against a device lacking a master file, with sponsor characterization on a defined battery accepted as a full substitute.
Wants cloud platform intermediaries eligible to hold master files, since they often control versions and deprecations.
Supports leaving care coordination, documentation and outreach agents outside device focus and wants that boundary preserved clearly.
Wants human-oversight checkpoints before irreversible actions verified as non-bypassable in the configuration actually deployed, not just documented.
Wants prompt-injection resistance evaluated across user input, retrieved EHR content and tool outputs.
Wants characterized failure envelopes showing the agent degrades to deferral or handoff when tools fail, rather than improvising.
Calls the paper a substantive, well-constructed foundation whose commitments match what responsible manufacturers already practise.
